properties.ch: The United States acquired Alaska from Russia. Presidential proclamation issued 20 June 1867. Alaska was considered an "unorganized territory" with no organized civil government.
The United States Congress established a civil government for Alaska. This act was limited and resulted in a partial organization of Alaska as a territory.
The state of Alaska was created from Alaska Territory by Presidential proclamation; Alaska Territory eliminated.
Alaska was fully organized as a territory in the United States.
The state of Alabama was created from Alabama Territory; Alabama Territory eliminated.

Surveyors demarcated the southern segment of the Alabama-Mississippi line, fixing the end point ten miles east of the mouth of the Pascagoula River. BALDWIN, MOBILE, and WASHINGTON lost to the state of Mississippi.
MARION's overlap of the state of Mississippi and TUSCALOOSA's overlap of the state of Mississippi ended.
The United States created Alabama Territory from the eastern half of Mississippi Territory.
TUSCALOOSA created by Alabama Territory from MONTGOMERY and Non-County Area 1; TUSCALOOSA overlapped non-county area in the state of Mississippi.
The state of Arkansas was created from Arkansas Territory; Arkansas Territory eliminated.

Survey of boundary between the Republic of Texas and the United States began. MILLER (original) officially became extinct and LAFAYETTE was eliminated from Texas when Texas claims to the area were upheld.

The United States created Arkansas Territory from Missouri Territory. Arkansas Territory included all of present Arkansas and part of present Oklahoma. Boundary between Arkansas Territory and Mexico remained unsettled.
Arkansas Territory was reduced in size when the western extent of the territory was moved to a line running forty miles west of the southwest corner of Missouri.

CLARK, CRAWFORD, LOVELEY, and MILLER lost to Indian lands when the treaty between the United States and Cherokee Indians established the western line of Arkansas Territory north of Red River along the eastern line of the Choctaw Cession.
The state of Arizona was created from Arizona Territory; Arizona Territory eliminated.
The United States created  Arizona Territory from the western portion of New Mexico Territory and a part of present Nevada.

State of Nevada gained parts of MOHAVE and PAH-UTE (extinct) when the United States transferred the portion of Arizona Territory lying between 37 degrees and 42 degrees of north latitude and west of 114 degrees west longitude to Nevada.
The state of California was admitted to the Union.

Between 1949 and 1959 (precise date unknown) SAN FRANCISCO gained a small area of the Alameda Naval Air Station when landfill expansion extended westward over the county line between SAN FRANCISCO and ALAMEDA in San Francisco Bay.
The state of Colorado was created from Colorado Territory; Colorado Territory eliminated.
The United States created Colorado Territory from Nebraska, New Mexico, and Utah Territories, and from the former Kansas Territory.
Connecticut became an independent state on 4 July 1776. The map depicts state boundaries as of 3 September 1783.

Connecticut ceded to the United States its claim to lands north and west of Pennsylvania and the Ohio River, except for a tract, lying in the northeast corner of present Ohio, known as the Connecticut Western Reserve.
Connecticut ceded the Western Reserve in present Ohio to the United States, and the area was incorporated into the Northwest Territory.
HARTFORD lost part of the town of Southwick (the "Southwick Jog") to HAMPSHIRE (Mass.) when the state boundary was adjusted.
The United States created an unnamed district from land ceded by Maryland and Virginia to be the seat of national government.

The federal government retroceded to Virginia all of the District of Columbia west of the Potomac River, including all of ALEXANDRIA (now ARLINGTON, Va.). ALEXANDRIA eliminated from the District of Columbia.

The three Lower Counties, of KENT, NEW CASTLE, and SUSSEX became an independent state on 4 July 1776. The name Delaware was formally adopted on 20 September 1776. The map depicts state boundaries as of 3 September 1783.

The United States created Dakota Territory from Nebraska Territory and unorganized federal territory; included all of present North Dakota, South Dakota, and parts of present Montana, Nebraska and Wyoming.

The United States created Idaho Territory from Dakota, Nebraska, and Washington Territories. Dakota Territory was reduced to the area of present North Dakota and South Dakota, plus a small area of present Nebraska.
Dakota Territory gained from Idaho Territory; included most of present Wyoming and a small area of about two square miles in present Montana that had been part of MADISON (Mont.).
The small remnant of Dakota Territory in present Montana again became non-county area when Wyoming Territory boundaries were established.
UNION lost small area to the state of Nebraska when the Missouri River changed course.
TRIPP created by Dakota Territory in present South Dakota from GREGORY, TODD (original, extinct), and Non-County Area (1); TRIPP included a small piece of present Nebraska.
Montana Territory gained the small remnant of Dakota Territory that remained between Montana and Wyoming Territories.

GREGORY, TRIPP, and TODD (original, extinct) each lost to the state of Nebraska. TODD implicitly gained part of Fort Randall Military Reserve, and the remaining part of the Military Reserve became part of the state of Nebraska.

The General Assembly of the newly proposed state of Deseret met on 2 Jul 1849. The state was to include almost all of Utah and parts of present Ariz., Cal., Colo., Ida., Nev., N.Mex., Ore., and Wyo., but proposal never gained support in U.S. Congress.

On 29 Oct 1782 New York ceded to the US any claim to territory west of the meridian of the western end of Lake Ontario, thereby defining its western boundary; the Erie Triangle in present Penn. is part of this cession. Map depicts area as of 3 Sep 1783.
The state of Florida was created from Florida Territory, with boundaries the same as those set in 1822; Florida Territory eliminated.

The United States created the Territory of Florida from the provinces of East and West Florida ceded by Spain to the United States. The territory had the same boundaries as the present state of Florida.
Spain ceded East Florida and West Florida (i.e., all territory east of the Perdido River) to the United States. Exchange of ratifications was delayed until 21 February 1821.
Georgia became an independent state on 4 July 1776. The map depicts state boundaries as of 3 September 1783.

The United States created Mississippi Territory. Georgia continued to claim this area under its colonial charter, and the federal act said that creation of the territory would not impair Georgia's claim.
Georgia ceded to the United States much of present Mississippi and Alabama. This area became unorganized federal territory and Georgia Western Lands were eliminated.
Gadsden Purchase settled the boundary dispute between the United States and Mexico and established the international line at its present location.
President McKinley signed a joint resolution of Congress annexing Hawaii to the United States.
The state of Hawaii was created from Hawaii Territory; Hawaii Territory eliminated.
The United States created the Territory of Hawaii.
The state of Iowa was created from Iowa Territory; Iowa Territory eliminated.
The United States created Iowa Territory from Wisconsin Territory.
The state of Idaho was created from Idaho Territory; Idaho Territory eliminated.
The United States created Idaho Territory from Dakota, Nebraska, and Washington Territories.
The United States created Montana Territory from Idaho Territory with boundaries identical to the state of Montana; Dakota Territory gained most of present Wyoming from Idaho Territory.
The United States created Wyoming Territory from Dakota, Idaho, and Utah Territories, and from part of ONEIDA.
The state of Illinois was created from Illinois Territory; Illinois Territory eliminated.
The United States created Illinois Territory from Indiana Territory.

The state of Indiana created from Illinois, Indiana, and Michigan Territories; EDWARDS exchanged small areas along the Wabash River with the state of Indiana, establishing the boundary between the present states of Illinois and Indiana.
The state of Indiana was created from Indiana Territory and small parts of Illinois and Michigan Territories.
The United States created Indiana Territory from the Northwest Territory; included all of present Illinois and Wisconsin, most of present Indiana, and parts of present Michigan, Minnesota, and Ohio.

The state of Ohio was created from the Northwest Territory and Indiana Territory. Indiana Territory gained remainder of the former Northwest Territory in present Michigan and Indiana; Northwest Territory eliminated.
The United States created Michigan Territory from Indiana Territory; WAYNE (Ind. Terr.) was effectively eliminated.
The United States created Illinois Territory from Indiana Territory.

Arkansas Territory was reduced in size when the western extent of the territory was moved to a line running forty miles west of the southwest corner of Missouri. Unorganized federal territory in present Oklahoma became known as Indian Territory.

Indian Territory gained from Arkansas Territory when the Treaty of Washington between the United States and Choctaw Indians definitively established the eastern line of the Choctaw Cession and affirmed Choctaw control of the area west of the line.
The United States created Oklahoma Territory from Indian Territory and unorganized federal territory (the Oklahoma panhandle or Public Land Strip).
Oklahoma Territory gained a portion of the Indian Territory, designated the Cherokee Outlet, under a treaty between the United States and the Cherokee Nation.
The state of Kansas was created from Kansas Territory; Kansas Territory eliminated.

Missouri and Kansas exchanged territory along the Missouri River from 40 degrees north latitude to the Kansas River. The change was made to accommodate shifts in the course of the Missouri River following the 1944 flood.
The United States created Kansas Territory from unorganized federal territory; included all of present Kansas and part of present Colorado.
The state of Kentucky was created from the Kentucky District of Virginia.
ROBERTSON (Tenn.) and SUMNER (Tenn.) gained from SIMPSON (Ky.) when surveyors re-marking the Kentucky-Tennessee boundary acted without authority and shifted the line around two small parcels.
The United States created the District of Louisiana from the part of the Louisiana Purchase north of 33 degrees north latitude, the limit of the present state of Louisiana.

The United States purchased Louisiana from France, taking formal possession 20 December 1803; boundaries were not clearly defined but unquestionably included the western half of the Mississippi drainage basin.
The State of Louisiana was created from Orleans Territory; Orleans Territory eliminated.
District of Louisiana renamed Louisiana Territory and detached from Indiana Territory; the territory included all of present Missouri.
Massachusetts, including the area of Maine, became an independent state on 4 July 1776. The map depicts state boundaries as of 3 September 1783.
Massachusetts gained part of the town of Southwick (the "Southwick Jog") that lay south of the Connecticut boundary and that had been annexed from Massachusetts in 1774.
Maine was separated from Massachusetts and admitted to the Union.
New York acquired the southwestern corner of Massachusetts, known as Boston Corner.

BRISTOL gained from NEWPORT (R.I.) and lost to PROVIDENCE (R.I.) when Massachusetts and Rhode Island implemented the U.S. Supreme Court settlement (31 December 1861) of their boundary to the Atlantic Ocean.
Maryland became an independent state on 4 July 1776. The map depicts state boundaries as of 3 September 1783.
The United States created an unnamed district from land ceded by Maryland and Virginia to be the seat of national government.
Maine was separated from Massachusetts and admitted to the Union.
The state of Michigan was created from Michigan Territory; boundary dispute with Ohio over the strip running from Indiana to Lake Erie was settled in favor of Ohio; Michigan Territory eliminated.

The new Michigan constitution redefined part of the interstate boundary with Wisconsin across the Upper Peninsula. GOGEBIC (Mich.) implicitly overlapped Wisconsin (IRON and VILAS Counties), but Wisconsin kept control of the disputed area.

Michigan took its 1909 boundary dispute with Wisconsin to the United States Supreme Court and expanded its scope by claiming more territory on the Upper Peninsula and more of the waters and islands of Green Bay.
The United States Supreme Court decided the dispute between Michigan and Wisconsin entirely in favor of Wisconsin; implicit overlaps of Wisconsin by DELTA, GOGEBIC, and IRON ended.
The United States created Michigan Territory from Indiana Territory.
The state of Indiana was created from Indiana Territory and small parts of Illinois and Michigan Territories.

The state of Illinois was created from Illinois Territory. Michigan Territory gained the former parts of Illinois and Indiana Territories in present Wisconsin and the Upper Peninsula of present Michigan.

Michigan Territory gained unorganized federal territory west of the Mississippi River, north of the state of Missouri, and east of the Missouri and White Earth Rivers, including present Iowa and parts of present Minnesota and North and South Dakota.
The United States created Wisconsin Territory from Michigan Territory.

The state of Minnesota was created from Minnesota Territory;  Minnesota Territory eliminated. The remainder of Minnesota Territory (west of the present state boundary) became unorganized federal territory.
The United States created Minnesota Territory from unorganized federal territory west of the Mississippi River (formerly part of Iowa Territory) and de facto Wisconsin Territory.
The state of Missouri was created from Missouri Territory, with all modern boundaries, except for the northwestern corner of the present state, which became unorganized federal territory.
The northwestern boundary of the state of Missouri was extended to the Missouri River, eliminating unorganized federal territory from Missouri.

Missouri legislature extended CLARK's boundary line north of the commonly accepted boundary between Missouri and Iowa Territory (the Indian boundary line established in 1816); the extension overlapped Iowa's VAN BUREN.

U.S. Supreme Court settled boundary dispute between Iowa and Missouri by rejecting both states' claims, choosing instead the commonly accepted boundary before the dispute arose and the present boundary between the two states.

Missouri and Kansas exchanged territory along the Missouri River from 40 degrees north latitude to the Kansas River. The change was made to accommodate shifts in the course of the Missouri River following the 1944 flood.
Louisiana Territory renamed Missouri Territory.

Area exchanged with British North America when a Convention of Commerce between Great Britain and the United States established 49 degrees north latitude, from the Lake of the Woods to the Rocky Mtns., as the northern boundary of the United States.
Non-County Area exchanged with Spain as a result of the Adams-Onis Treaty with Spain on 22 February 1819.

HEMPSTEAD created by Missouri Territory from ARKANSAS and non-county area. Uncertainty of boundary between Mexico and the U.S. resulted in competing claims to area in Texas. Act passed 15 December 1818, took effect 1 June 1819.
The United States created Arkansas Territory from that part of Missouri Territory south of the parallel of 36 degrees, 30 minutes north latitude.
The state of Mississippi was created from Mississippi Territory; Mississippi Territory was eliminated.
Surveyors demarcated the southern segment of the Alabama-Mississippi line, fixing the end point ten miles east of the mouth of the Pascagoula River.
The United States created Mississippi Territory in parts of present Mississippi and Alabama.
Mississippi Territory gained unorganized federal territory south of Tennessee (northern portions of present Mississippi and Alabama).
The state of Louisiana was created from Orleans Territory; Orleans Territory eliminated. The area encompassed by PASCAGOULA (Orleans Terr.) was formally added to Mississippi Territory on 14 May 1812.
The United States created Alabama Territory from the eastern half of Mississippi Territory.
The state of Montana created from Montana Territory and to the Union by Presidential proclamation; Montana Territory eliminated.

The United States created Montana Territory from Idaho Territory; boundaries were identical to the state of Montana, except for a small area of about two square miles (formerly part of MADISON) that became part of Dakota Territory.
Montana Territory gained the small remnant of Dakota Territory that remained between Montana and Wyoming Territories.
Treaty of Guadalupe-Hidalgo ended the war between Mexico and the United States. Area ceded by Mexico became Unorganized Federal Territory (non-county area) in the United States.

The United States created Utah Territory from the territory ceded by Mexico in the Treaty of Guadalupe-Hidalgo (1848), from territory to be purchased from the state of Texas in December 1850, and from unorganized federal territory.
North Carolina became an independent state on 4 July 1776. The map depicts state boundaries as of 3 September 1783.
Congress accepted North Carolina's cession of its western lands (i.e. present Tennessee).
The state of North Dakota was created from the Dakota Territory; Dakota Territory eliminated.
The state of Nebraska was created from Nebraska Territory; Nebraska Territory eliminated.
DAKOTA gained small area from UNION (S.D.) in Dakota Territory when the Missouri River changed course.
TRIPP created by Dakota Territory in present South Dakota from GREGORY, TODD (original, extinct), and Non-County Area (1); TRIPP included a small piece of present Nebraska.
The state of Nebraska gained the area between 43 degrees north latitude and the Keya Paha and Niobrara Rivers from Dakota Territory. This territory became Non-County Area 8 in Nebraska.
CLAY (S.D.) officially gained an island in the Missouri River from DIXON (Neb.); voters approved the gain 1006 to 25.

The United States created Nebraska Territory from unorganized federal territory. Nebraska Territory included all of present Nebraska and parts of present Colorado, Montana, North Dakota, South Dakota, and Wyoming.
Nebraska Territory lost to creation of Colorado Territory; Nebraska Territory included all of present Nebraska and parts of present Montana, North Dakota, South Dakota, and Wyoming.
Nebraska Territory gained from Utah and Washington Territories, lost to creation of Dakota Territory. Nebraska Territory included most of present Nebraska and part of Wyoming.
Nebraska Territory lost the area in present Wyoming to creation of Idaho Territory.
New Hampshire became an independent state on 4 July 1776. The map depicts state boundaries as of 3 September 1783.
New Jersey became an independent state on 4 July 1776. The map depicts state boundaries as of 3 September 1783.
The state of New Mexico was created from New Mexico Territory; New Mexico Territory eliminated.

The United States created New Mexico Territory from Unorganized Federal Territory (land ceded by Mexico to the United States in the Treaty of Guadalupe-Hidalgo) and from territory purchased from the state of Texas.
The territory acquired by the United States in the Gadsden Purchase was officially added to New Mexico Territory.
The United States created Colorado Territory from New Mexico, Utah, Kansas, and Nebraska Territories.
The United States created Arizona Territory from New Mexico Territory.
The state of Nevada was created from Nevada Territory and admitted to the Union by presidential proclamation.
Nevada Territory gained from Utah Territory and from Arizona Territory.
The United States created Nevada Territory from Utah Territory.
Nevada Territory gained from Utah Territory.
The U.S. created the Territory of the United States Northwest of the River Ohio (Northwest Territory) from unorganized federal territory.
WASHINGTON created by the Northwest Territory from non-county area and part of the Western Reserve. This implicit challenge to Connecticut's authority in the Western Reserve went unanswered.
WAYNE (Northwest Terr., extinct) created by the Northwest Territory from HAMILTON (Ohio), KNOX (Ind.), and non-county area.
The United States created Indiana Territory from the Northwest Territory; included all of present Illinois and Wisconsin, most of present Indiana, and parts of present Michigan, Minnesota, and Ohio.
New York became an independent state on 4 July 1776, and Vermont declared its independence from New York on 15 January 1777. The map depicts state boundaries as of 3 September 1783.
New York acquired the southwestern corner of Massachusetts (Boston Corner).
The state of Ohio was created from the Northwest Territory and Indiana Territory.
The state of Oklahoma was created from Oklahoma Territory and Indian Territory; Oklahoma Territory and Indian Territory eliminated.
The United States created Oklahoma Territory from Indian Territory and unorganized federal territory (the Oklahoma panhandle or Public Land Strip).
Oklahoma Territory gained a portion of the Indian Territory, designated the Cherokee Outlet, under a treaty between the United States and the Cherokee Nation.

The United States created Orleans Territory from that portion of Louisiana south of the parallel of 33 degrees north latitude, west of the Mississippi River, and south of Mississippi Territory east of the river.
Based on American exploration of the Northwest, the United States claimed the Oregon Country, an area west of the 1803 Louisiana Purchase that was not specifically defined.
The state of Oregon was created from Oregon Territory; Oregon Territory eliminated.
The United States created the Territory of Oregon, encompassing all of present Oregon, Washington, and Idaho, and parts of present Montana and Wyoming.
The United States created Washington Territory from Oregon Territory.
The Oregon Boundary Treaty between the United States and Great Britain ended joint occupancy of the Oregon Country.
Pennsylvania became an independent state on 4 July 1776. The map depicts state boundaries as of 3 September 1783.
Pennsylvania purchased from the federal government the Erie Triangle, a small area immediately north of Pennsylvania and west of New York, giving Pennsylvania an outlet to Lake Erie.
Rhode Island became an independent state on 4 July 1776. The map depicts state boundaries as of 3 September 1783.

NEWPORT lost to BRISTOL (Mass.) and PROVIDENCE gained from BRISTOL (Mass.) when Massachusetts and Rhode Island implemented the U. S. Supreme Court settlement (31 December 1861) of their boundary to the Atlantic Ocean.
South Carolina became an independent state on 4 July 1776. The map depicts state boundaries as of 3 September 1783.
The state of South Dakota was created from the Dakota Territory; Dakota Territory eliminated.
CLAY (S.D.) officially gained an island in the Missouri River from DIXON (Neb.); voters approved the gain 1006 to 25.
The United States created the Territory of the United States South of the River Ohio (Southwest Territory), covering the territory ceded in April 1790 by North Carolina (area of present Tennessee).
The state of Tennessee was created from the Territory of the United States South of the River Ohio (Southwest Territory); Southwest Territory eliminated.
ROBERTSON (Tenn.) and SUMNER (Tenn.) gained from SIMPSON (Ky.) when surveyors remarking the Kentucky-Tennessee boundary acted without authority and shifted the line around two small parcels.
Texas declared its independence from Mexico.
The state of Texas was admitted to the Union; Republic of Texas eliminated.
State of Texas sold land in present Colorado, Kansas, New Mexico, Oklahoma, and Wyoming to the United States.

GREER eliminated from Texas when U.S. Supreme Court ruled that GREER was not within the boundaries of Texas, but was under the jurisdiction of the United States. GREER became a county in Oklahoma Territory on 4 May 1896.
The boundary from Lake of the Woods to the Rocky Mtns. between the United States and the British possessions was unsettled.

All of present Illinois became unorganized federal territory when Virginia ceded its charter claims to the area to the United States. Other claims by Connecticut, Massachusetts, and New York to the area west of Pennsylvania were eliminated by 1786.

The U.S. accepted Connecticut's cession of lands north and west of Pennsylvania and the Ohio River, except for a tract (Western Reserve) lying north of 41 degrees north latitude (Connecticut's southern line) and extending 120 miles west of Pennsylvania.
Congress accepted North Carolina's cession of its western lands (i.e. present Tennessee).

Georgia ceded to the United States all territory south of North Carolina and Tennessee, east of the Mississippi River, north of 31 degrees north latitude and west of the present limit of Georgia. The area became unorganized federal territory.

Part of the Upper Peninsula of present Michigan and the extreme eastern part of present Wisconsin became unorganized federal territory when the state of Indiana was created from Indiana, Illinois, and Michigan Territories.

The state of Missouri was created from part of Missouri Territory; Missouri Territory eliminated and all that part of the former territory north and west of the state of Missouri became unorganized federal territory.
The unorganized federal territory lost to the creation of Indian Territory.
Unorganized federal territory lost to Michigan Territory.
MO Non-County Area 28 created from unorganized federal territory, and attached to CLAY "for civil and military purposes." MO Non-County Area 12 gained from unorganized federal territory.
The state of Iowa was created from Iowa Territory. All of the former Territory north and west of the present state became unorganized federal territory.
Unorganized federal territory lost to creation of Minnesota Territory; all of present North and South Dakota west of the Missouri and White Earth Rivers remained unorganized federal territory.
Unorganized federal territory lost to creation of Utah Territory.
The state of Texas sold land in present Kansas, Colorado, New Mexico, Oklahoma, and Wyoming to the United States.
The United States created Kansas Territory and Nebraska Territory from unorganized federal territory.

The state of Minnesota was created from Minnesota Territory; Minnesota Territory eliminated. That part of present North and South Dakota east of the Missouri and White Earth Rivers became unorganized federal territory.

Area within present Colorado that had been part of Kansas Terr. temporarily reverted to unorganized federal territory until official creation of Colorado Terr. on 28 Feb 1861. State of Kansas was admitted to the union this date; Kansas Terr. eliminated.
The United States created Colorado Territory from Nebraska, New Mexico, and Utah Territories, and from the former Kansas Territory. Boundaries were identical to the state of Colorado.
The United States created Dakota Territory from Nebraska Territory and Unorganized Federal Territory.
The state of Utah was created from Utah Territory; Utah Territory eliminated.

The United States created Utah Territory from the territory ceded by Mexico in the Treaty of Guadalupe-Hidalgo (1848), from territory to be purchased from the state of Texas in December 1850, and from unorganized federal territory.
The United States created Colorado Territory from Nebraska, New Mexico, and Utah Territories, and from the former Kansas Territory.
The United States created Nevada Territory from Utah Territory. Utah Territory also lost to Nebraska Territory when Nebraska Territory gained area in present Wyoming from Utah Territory.
Nevada Territory gained from Utah Territory.
The state of Nevada gained from Utah Territory.
The United States created Wyoming Territory from Dakota, Idaho, and Utah Territories.
Virginia became an independent state on 4 July 1776. The map depicts state boundaries as of 3 September 1783.

Virginia ceded to the United States its 1609 charter claims to territory "northwestward of the river Ohio," thereby setting the north bank of the Ohio River as the northern and northwestern limit for present Kentucky and West Virginia.

The United States created an unnamed federal district (now the District of Columbia) from MONTGOMERY and PRINCE GEORGES in Maryland and from FAIRFAX in Virginia to be the seat of the federal government.
The state of Kentucky was created from the Kentucky District of Virginia.
The District of Columbia ceded ALEXANDRIA (now ARLINGTON) to Virginia.
The state of West Virginia was formally separated from Virginia and admitted to the Union. Most of West Virginia had been effectively independent of Virginia since June 1861.
Virginia lost BERKELEY (W.Va.) to West Virginia.
The state of Virginia lost JEFFERSON (W.Va.) to West Virginia.

Vermont declared its independence from New York in 1777. Although not recognized as a separate state by the Continental Congress, Vermont functioned as an independent republic until statehood in 1791. Map depicts Vermont boundaries as of 3 Sep 1783.
The state of Vermont was admitted to the Union. The boundary with New York was settled by a joint commission before statehood.
The state of Washington was created from Washington Territory; Washington Territory eliminated.
The United States created Washington Territory from Oregon Territory; included all of present Washington and parts of present Idaho and Montana.
Washington Territory gained non-county area when the state of Oregon was created from Oregon Territory. Non-County Area 2 included parts of present Idaho, Montana, and Wyoming.
Nebraska Territory gained part of SHOSHONE (Idaho).
The United States created Idaho Territory from Dakota, Nebraska, and Washington Territories.

The state of Wisconsin was created from Wisconsin Territory. The area in present Minnesota between the Mississippi River and the state of Wisconsin continued as de facto Wisconsin Territory until the creation of Minnesota Territory on 3 March 1849.

An overlap was created when Wisconsin appeared to gain islands north of the Rock Island Passage from Michigan when the U.S. Supreme Court described the Wis.-Mich. boundary through Lake Michigan and Green Bay and introduced some unintentional errors.
Dispute between Michigan and Wisconsin ended when the U.S. Supreme Court decreed the precise course of the revised Michigan-Wisconsin boundary through Green Bay and Lake Michigan.
The United States created Wisconsin Territory from Michigan Territory; included all of present Wisconsin, Iowa, and Minnesota; and parts of present North and South Dakota.
The United States created Iowa Territory from Wisconsin Territory, encompassing all of Wisconsin Territory west of the Mississippi River.

The state of Wisconsin was created from Wisconsin Territory. The area in present Minnesota between the Mississippi River and the state of Wisconsin continued as de facto Wisconsin Territory until the creation of Minnesota Territory on 3 March 1849.
The state of West Virginia was formally separated from Virginia and admitted to the Union. Most of West Virginia had been effectively independent of Virginia since June 1861.
BERKELEY was separated from Virginia and became a county in the state of West Virginia.
JEFFERSON was separated from Virginia and became a county in the state of West Virginia.
The state of Wyoming was created from Wyoming Territory; Wyoming Territory eliminated.
The United States created Wyoming Territory with present boundaries from Dakota, Idaho, and Utah Territories.
